angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 2,263,112 km at 38.93 pc = 0.78 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 95168: distance 38.926 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.007), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 38.926 +/- 0.272 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 25.0011 +/- 0.2449 mas (same row, RUWE 2.74), 102.1 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 3.253 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 95168: radius 3.253 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 30.207 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.044) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 2,263,112 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 7508 +/- 180 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 95168: effective temperature 7508 +/- 180 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.029) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 95168: effective temperature 7508 +/- 180 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.029) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Pulkovo spectrophotometric catalogue, table 5 (320-1080 nm, 2.5 nm steps, 10 nm resolution, absolute flux in W m^-2 m^-1)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
